Running log. Morning: premeditatio malorum, five minutes, before the kettle. Evening: the Seneca review from *De Ira* III.36, "When the light has been taken away and my wife, long aware of my habit, has fallen silent, I examine my entire day." Aoife is not silent, but she has learnt to let me be for ten minutes.

Three questions for the evening review, straight from Seneca: What bad habit did I cure today? What fault did I resist? In what respect am I better?

- **2025-01-06.** Back to school. Morning: imagined the photocopier dying before the 9:10 class. It died at 9:04. Smug, for once.
- **2025-01-07.** Evening review: snapped at Cian in 2nd year for the third time about his phone. Fault not resisted.
- **2025-01-12.** Epictetus, *Enchiridion* ch. 1: "Some things are up to us and some are not." Wrote the two lists on an index card. The Leaving Cert results are not up to me; my feedback on their mock essays is.
- **2025-01-19.** Cold shower, 30 seconds. Voluntary discomfort (Seneca, Letter 18, live poor for a few days). Lasted 30 seconds and swore for 25 of them.
- **2025-01-26.** Missed four evening reviews in a row. Bed by 11 matters more than the review; see [[Sleep]].
- **2025-02-02.** Marcus, the "view from above": walked up Killiney Hill and looked at the bay. Felt my staffroom grievance about the timetable shrink to its proper size.
- **2025-02-20.** Fasted until 6pm. Irritable by 2pm, not enlightened. Will not repeat on a teaching day.
- **2025-03-01.** Tally since 6 Jan: evening review done 41 of 54 nights. Morning one 47 of 54.
- **2025-03-15.** Combined the evening review with three lines of thanks, as in [[Gratitude list]]. Seems to stick better that way.
- **2025-04-04.** Started doing ten minutes of the stretching from [[朝のヨガ]] before the morning premeditatio. Body first, then the bad news.

Notes to self:
- The book club is good for talking about Stoicism, this log is for doing it. Don't confuse them ([[Book club Meditations]]).
- Ward Farnsworth, *The Practicing Stoic* (2018), p. 21, on the dichotomy of control. Better than any of the self-help versions.
